citations.assertion: Previously cited subject; relationship scope in the father assessment. The original 1820 Smith County census, page 58, household 716, has James Glasgow with one male under 10, one male 10–15 and one male 26–44; females comprise one under 10 and one 16–25. The age-band reading follows the standard column order and is consistent with the county transcription; this manuscript leaf has no column headings. The original 1840 page 270 has a James household with males 5–9, 10–14 and 60–69, two females 15–19 and one female 40–49. Those older male bands fit the circa-1776 James account, but do not identify him uniquely. An unnamed 1820 boy could fit Wesley’s estimated 1818 birth; no 1840 male 20–29 appears in this household. Wesley could already have left home, so that absence does not exclude paternity. The 1820 page groups G surnames and is not evidence that adjacent lines were physical neighbours. Wesley-2476’s selected father James-2492 remains Possible at 35%; James-2492’s own father James-634 remains Confident at 94%. The census age slots are compatible household evidence, not named kin or independent birth entries. No new parent, exact vital date, maternal attachment, profile merger or confidence gain follows. The cited indexes and their newly inspected originals describe the same underlying events and are not independent witnesses.
